newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Islamist party says studying boycott call.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Islamist party says studying boycott call.

text.p: Jordan's Moslem parliamentary party the Islamic Action Front (IAF) said on Saturday it would discuss with other opposition groups whether or not to boycott elections due later this year.
The IAF, responding to a call for a boycott by the powerful Moslem Brotherhood, said it was studying the issue.

"We hope the government realises the seriousness of the matter," the party said in a statement after a three hour meeting on Saturday night. "It has turned a deaf ear to our advice and warnings...(and) marginalised the role of political parties and parliament."
Some IAF members have said bluntly they oppose the Brotherhood's demand for a pull-out from Jordan's first elections since it signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994.
The Islamists want the peace accord annulled but despite holding one-fifth of seats after the 1993 elections they were unable to block its parliamentary ratification.
This year's elections are due to be held by November. The government has yet to set a date for the polls but has promised they will be held on time and will be fair.
"The meeting decided to continue studying (the boycott call) with opposition parties and national powers in the country," the statement said.
It did not say when the party expected to announce its final decision.

The statement called on the government to review recent amendments to Jordan's press and election laws issued during parliament's recess, and look at "the level of general freedoms" as a first step towards resolving an impasse with the opposition.

Opposition groups say the amended press law stifles all criticism of the government and the one-vote system for electors, as opposed to a voting list used in 1989 elections, favours tribal candidates who usually support the government.
